page_title: BBC Learning English - English at Work / The Appraisal
title: The Appraisal
topic: Language to use in an appraisal
description:
It's time for Anna's appraisal - a chance to review how things are going and to set some challenges for the year ahead. But will Anna like what Paul has to say? Maybe news about Rachel will put a smile on her face?
This episode focuses on what to say when you have an appraisal at work.
phrases: What has gone well for you this year? Give me some examples.
And what didn't go so well?
What should you do more of?
Let's look ahead and set some objectives.

listening_challenge.question: As part of Anna's objectives, what has she been asked to develop? The answer is at the bottom of the transcript below.
listening_challenge.answer: As part of Anna's objectives, what has she been asked to develop? - Plastic vegetables.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Could I have a word Anna, in my office?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Hello again. I wonder what Paul wants to say to Anna? Could it have something to do with Rachel, the pen thief - or is it just to do with biscuits?! Let's find out.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Have a seat… so well done for speaking to her. Stealing all those pens from the office was the final straw.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: She was stealing straws?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: No, no. It was the final thing that she did wrong – and it meant disciplinary action. I've had to 'let her go' – in other words, sack her.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, so she's gone. But what is Mr Socrates going to say? She was his best employee.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Leave it with me. I’m sure he'll understand…I hope. Now, I wanted to speak to you about your appraisal.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: My appraisal?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, we do it every year. It's a chance to talk about you, talk about the highs and lows of the past year and look forward.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Highs and lows? But I haven't been walking up any hills.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: No Anna! He means your appraisal is about reviewing your performance and setting objectives for the year ahead.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: I see. But what are objectives?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
These are tasks for you to do, to try and improve your performance and skills and help the business. Here are the questions you’re likely to hear in an appraisal: 
What's gone well for you this year?
What didn't go so well?
What should you do more of?
Let's look ahead and set some objectives.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. Thanks. So Paul, when shall we have this, err, appraisal?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: If you've time, we could make a start now?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh OK. So I need to think about my performance first?

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Exactly. What has gone well for you this year?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well I guess I've just done my job.

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Anna! This is your chance to sell yourself. Think about the deals you've made, the people you've managed, that sort of thing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Right. Well, I did complete two big contracts for the Imperial Lemon…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: You've had plenty of compliments for that. You seem to have a zest for selling!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, right… and then there was dealing with Mr Ingle in the warehouse.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Yes, that's a good example of dealing with difficult staff. And what didn't go so well?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Well… erm… working with Rachel… and cold calling I suppose. That wasn’t easy.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Ah yes. But you soon warmed up! And what should you do more of?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err, erm…

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: It's a tricky question Anna – but don't be ashamed about admitting things that you feel you could improve on. Nobody's perfect! Think about skills you'd like to improve.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh OK. Well Paul, I guess I could… develop some ideas for new products? Continue to work on the European marketing strategy... sell more Imperial Lemons… err…

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: That's enough Anna!  If you do all that, you'll put me out of a job!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, I don't want to do that!

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Now let's look ahead and set some objectives. Biscuit?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Biscuits as an objective? Oh I see…no thanks.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: We've all got to improve our sales targets so I'm asking all the team to make an extra ten sales deals this year.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Oh, ten, that’s a lot.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: It is - but I know you can do it. And you mentioned developing new products, well I'd like you to do just that – but not plastic fruit, I'd like you to develop a plastic vegetable. Potato, carrot, that sort of thing.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Gosh. Well, OK.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: Oh and one more thing. Could you help Denise sort out the stationery cupboard? It's a right mess.

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Err...

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text:
That's a lot of objectives for Anna. She's got her work cut out for the next year. Appraisals are a good time to review your work and plan what you are going to do next. Here's a reminder of the kind of questions your manager may ask you:
What has gone well for you this year? Give me some examples.
What didn't go so well?
What should you do more of?
Let's look ahead and set some objectives.

transcript.speaker: Paul
transcript.text: So if you could write up your appraisal and have it back to me by Friday?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Of course Paul. Thanks. See you later.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Oh hi Anna. Are you still on for dinner on Friday?

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Yes Tom!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: What's going on?!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: A mouse… a mouse! I've just seen a mouse running out of the stationery office.

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Was he stealing the pens?!

transcript.speaker: Denise
transcript.text: It's no joke. Quick…there he goes!

transcript.speaker: Tom
transcript.text: Leave him to me! Oh… oww!

transcript.speaker: Anna
transcript.text: Tom… Tom? Are you ok?

transcript.speaker: Narrator
transcript.text: Uh oh! What’s happened to Tom? Has he broken something? Join us next time to find out. Bye!
